name: proof-command-then-you
about: QA proofs (docs/decisions/2026-10-18-qa-proofs.md), the command kind passing, with a manual check left. The build's proof: a command (the merge commit is on main: the runner runs it fenced in a fresh checkout of main, with LOOP_MERGE_SHA) and a manual check. At merge the thread says the loop checks the command itself, then the user looks. The runner's proof pass runs the command; it passes, so only the user's check is left: the thread gets the ask, mentioning the approver with what to look at and the Verified / Reopen buttons. Verified moves it to done.

proof.run: git cat-file -e "$LOOP_MERGE_SHA^{commit}" && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$LOOP_MERGE_SHA" HEAD && echo "main has $LOOP_MERGE_SHA"

proof.look: the pairing code on a phone: readable at arm's length

messages.text: #1 Pairing code size: Merged — the loop checks it itself: command: `git cat-file -e .*`\. <https://github.com/sandbox/demo/pull/101\|sandbox/demo#101> merged as `[0-9a-f]{7}`; watching main's CI\.\nThen your check: look at the pairing code on a phone: readable at arm's length\.\nIt is verified when every automatic check passes
